{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a1b2c3d4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1D GP Surrogate Predictions\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook demonstrates `plot_gp_predictions_1D`, which visualizes the GP surrogate model by sweeping each input parameter individually while holding all other parameters fixed. This is useful for understanding how sensitive the surrogate is to each dimension and for sanity-checking the GP fit in higher-dimensional problems where 2D contour plots are unavailable.\n",
    "\n",
    "For each dimension the plot shows:\n",
    "- **GP predictive mean** as a function of that parameter\n",
    "- **Uncertainty band** (±2σ) around the mean\n",
    "- **Training data** projected onto that parameter axis\n",
    "- **Vertical dashed line** marking the reference value\n",
    "\n",
    "The reference point is typically the surrogate maximum, obtained with `find_max_surrogate`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "b2c3d4e5",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from functools import partial\n",
    "from scipy.stats import multivariate_normal\n",
    "from sklearn import preprocessing\n",
    "\n",
    "import alabi\n",
    "import alabi.visualization as vis\n",
    "from alabi.core import SurrogateModel\n",
    "\n",
    "from matplotlib import rcParams\n",
    "# rcParams['font.family'] = 'serif'\n",
    "# rcParams['text.usetex'] = True\n",
    "\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c3d4e5f6",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Define a 4D Gaussian likelihood\n",
    "\n",
    "We use a 4-dimensional correlated Gaussian as the test likelihood. This is a natural target for `plot_gp_predictions_1D` — with 4 parameters a 2D contour plot can only show pairwise projections, but the 1D slices give a direct view of how each dimension contributes to the surrogate surface."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "d4e5f6a7",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "ndim = 4\n",
    "\n",
    "# True peak at the origin with a moderately correlated covariance\n",
    "mean = np.zeros(ndim)\n",
    "cov  = np.array([\n",
    "    [1.00,  0.60,  0.30, -0.20],\n",
    "    [0.60,  1.00,  0.10,  0.40],\n",
    "    [0.30,  0.10,  1.00,  0.50],\n",
    "    [-0.20, 0.40,  0.50,  1.00],\n",
    "])\n",
    "\n",
    "lnlike = partial(multivariate_normal.logpdf, mean=mean, cov=cov)\n",
    "\n",
    "bounds = [(-4., 4.)] * ndim\n",
    "param_names = [r\"$\\theta_1$\", r\"$\\theta_2$\", r\"$\\theta_3$\", r\"$\\theta_4$\"]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e5f6a7b8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Train the surrogate model\n",
    "\n",
    "First we'll compute some initial training samples"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "f6a7b8c9",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "sm = SurrogateModel(\n",
    "    lnlike_fn=lnlike,\n",
    "    bounds=bounds,\n",
    "    param_names=param_names,\n",
    "    savedir=\"results/gp_predictions_1d\",\n",
    "    verbose=False,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "sm.init_samples(ntrain=40, sampler=\"lhs\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6c1e487b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Here we will scale the input data using a minmax scaler so that $\\theta_i \\in [0,1]$ using the option:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "theta_scaler=preprocessing.MinMaxScaler()\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "Now, since $\\theta_i$ span [0,1], we might expect the length scales of the variation to be around ~0.1. We will set the length scale hyperparameter range to be between [0.1, 1], or in log scale:\n",
    "```python\n",
    "gp_scale_rng=[-1,1]\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "We will also set the amplitude range of the fit to be near the same order of magnitude as the variance in the training data"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "35bf4830",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "(np.float64(18410.313443996398), np.float64(4.265061182628903))"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 4,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "np.var(sm.y_train), np.log10(np.var(sm.y_train))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "33f49cbb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The log variance is around ~4, so we will set the GP amplitude bounds to be around this value. The length scale bounds are set to be fairly wide, but we will scale the inputs to be between 0 and 1, which should help with optimization.\n",
    "```python\n",
    "gp_amp_rng=[3.,5.]\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "f6f08d76",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Initialized GP with squared exponential kernel.\n",
      "Successfully initialized GP on attempt 1\n",
      "Evaluating 100 hyperparameter candidates using 5-fold CV...\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      " 30%|███       | 18/60 [00:01<00:04, 10.45it/s]"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Evaluating 100 hyperparameter candidates using 5-fold CV...\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      " 65%|██████▌   | 39/60 [00:04<00:02,  9.35it/s]"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Evaluating 100 hyperparameter candidates using 5-fold CV...\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      " 98%|█████████▊| 59/60 [00:07<00:00,  9.11it/s]"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Evaluating 100 hyperparameter candidates using 5-fold CV...\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "100%|██████████| 60/60 [00:08<00:00,  7.47it/s]"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Caching model to results/gp_predictions_1d/surrogate_model...\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "sm.init_gp(\n",
    "    kernel=\"ExpSquaredKernel\",\n",
    "    fit_amp=True,\n",
    "    fit_mean=True,\n",
    "    fit_white_noise=False,\n",
    "    white_noise=-12,\n",
    "    gp_opt_method=\"l-bfgs-b\",\n",
    "    theta_scaler=preprocessing.MinMaxScaler(),\n",
    "    gp_scale_rng=[-1.,1.], \n",
    "    gp_amp_rng=[3.,5.],\n",
    ")\n",
    "sm.active_train(\n",
    "    niter=60,\n",
    "    algorithm=\"bape\",\n",
    "    gp_opt_freq=20,\n",
    "    obj_opt_method=\"nelder-mead\",\n",
    "    nopt=3,\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c9d0e1f2",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Plot 1D GP predictions\n",
    "\n",
    "Call `plot_gp_predictions_1D` directly, passing the surrogate maximum as the reference point. Each panel sweeps one parameter across its full range while the remaining parameters are held fixed at `theta_max`. The true log-likelihood (black dashed line) is overplotted for comparison.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "d0e1f2a3",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Saving to  results/gp_predictions_1d/gp_predictions_1D.png\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1500x800 with 6 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from IPython.display import display\n",
    "\n",
    "theta_plot = np.zeros(sm.ndim)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig = vis.plot_gp_predictions_1D(\n",
    "    sm,\n",
    "    theta=theta_plot,  \n",
    "    ngrid=150,\n",
    "    nsigma=2,\n",
    "    title=\"GP predictions at surrogate maximum\",\n",
    "    savedir=\"results/gp_predictions_1d\",\n",
    "    show=False,\n",
    "    ylim=[-100, 0],\n",
    "    plot_samples=10,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Overplot the true log-likelihood on each panel\n",
    "ngrid = 150\n",
    "for dim in range(sm.ndim):\n",
    "    ax = fig.axes[dim]\n",
    "    xarr = np.linspace(sm.bounds[dim][0], sm.bounds[dim][1], ngrid)\n",
    "    sweep = np.tile(theta_plot, (ngrid, 1))\n",
    "    sweep[:, dim] = xarr\n",
    "    true_y = np.array([sm.true_log_likelihood(t) for t in sweep])\n",
    "    ax.plot(xarr, true_y, color=\"r\", lw=1.5, ls=\"--\", label=\"true\")\n",
    "    ax.legend(fontsize=10, loc=\"best\")\n",
    "\n",
    "display(fig)\n",
    "plt.close(fig)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e1f2a3b4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Use a custom reference point\n",
    "\n",
    "Any point in parameter space can serve as the reference. `find_max_surrogate` runs multi-start optimization to locate the parameter values where the GP predictive mean is highest. This is a natural reference point for the 1D slices — it shows a cross-section through the region the surrogate model considers most likely."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "bc23b9db",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Surrogate maximum:\n",
      "  $\\theta_1$ = 0.0306\n",
      "  $\\theta_2$ = 0.0038\n",
      "  $\\theta_3$ = -0.1694\n",
      "  $\\theta_4$ = -0.1503\n",
      "\n",
      "Surrogate log-likelihood at maximum: -2.2849\n",
      "True log-likelihood at maximum:      -2.2847\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "theta_max, y_max = sm.find_max_surrogate(nopt=20)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Surrogate maximum:\")\n",
    "for name, val in zip(param_names, theta_max):\n",
    "    print(f\"  {name} = {val:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"\\nSurrogate log-likelihood at maximum: {y_max:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"True log-likelihood at maximum:      {lnlike(theta_max):.4f}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "f2a3b4c5",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Best training point:\n",
      "  $\\theta_1$ = 0.0306\n",
      "  $\\theta_2$ = 0.0038\n",
      "  $\\theta_3$ = -0.1694\n",
      "  $\\theta_4$ = -0.1503\n",
      "\n",
      "Observed log-likelihood: -2.3056\n",
      "Saving to  results/gp_predictions_1d/gp_predictions_1D_surrogate_max.png\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",

       "<Figure size 1500x800 with 6 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "print(\"Best training point:\")\n",
    "for name, val in zip(param_names, theta_max):\n",
    "    print(f\"  {name} = {val:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"\\nObserved log-likelihood: {np.max(sm.y()):.4f}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "fig = vis.plot_gp_predictions_1D(\n",
    "    sm,\n",
    "    theta=theta_max,\n",
    "    ngrid=150,\n",
    "    nsigma=2,\n",
    "    title=\"GP predictions at surrogate maximum\",\n",
    "    savedir=\"results/gp_predictions_1d\",\n",
    "    savename=\"gp_predictions_1D_surrogate_max.png\",\n",
    "    show=False,\n",
    "    ylim=[-100, 0],\n",
    "    plot_samples=10,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Overplot the true log-likelihood on each panel\n",
    "ngrid = 150\n",
    "for dim in range(sm.ndim):\n",
    "    ax = fig.axes[dim]\n",
    "    xarr = np.linspace(sm.bounds[dim][0], sm.bounds[dim][1], ngrid)\n",
    "    sweep = np.tile(theta_max, (ngrid, 1))\n",
    "    sweep[:, dim] = xarr\n",
    "    true_y = np.array([sm.true_log_likelihood(t) for t in sweep])\n",
    "    ax.plot(xarr, true_y, color=\"r\", lw=1.5, ls=\"--\", label=\"true\")\n",
    "    ax.legend(fontsize=10, loc=\"best\")\n",
    "\n",
    "display(fig)\n",
    "plt.close(fig)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a3b4c5d6",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### Call via `sm.plot`\n",
    "\n",
    "`plot_gp_predictions_1D` is also integrated into `SurrogateModel.plot`. When called this way the reference point is automatically set to the surrogate maximum via `find_max_surrogate`. This function can be called using\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "sm.plot(plots=[\"gp_predictions_1D\"], show=True)\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9ccff1de",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### When is this diagnostic useful?\n",
    "\n",
    "Let's try another example where we don't scale the training data and bound the length scales to very small values in the range [0.0001, 0.01], or in log scale:\n",
    "```python\n",
    "gp_scale_rng=[-4,-2]\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5926f463",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "From the 1D diagnostic plot, we see that the prediction uncertainty is much larger and the mean prediction deviates quite a bit from the true model. Looking at some of the individual functions sampled from the GP, we can see that this high prediction variance is due to many of the functions being very \"wiggly\" or over-fitting to the data, which is an indication that the length scales of the fit are too small and the prior range `gp_scale_rng` needs to be adjusted.  "
   ]
  },
